messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Problem with lkj_corr
parts:
On Friday, February 19, 2016 at 11:21:37 AM UTC-5, Eric Innocents EBOULET wrote:
Hi Users'stan.

I'm writing hierarchical model to models response and response time defining in Rstan_Code.pdf. To do this, I'm writing model in ModelTimeResponse.stan. 
I you  think my model is OK, is it possible to explain why I obtain an errorr.

The screenshot is an informational message rather than an error. It says that there were 5 out of thousands of iterations where a correlation matrix in your model evaluated to

| 1 -1 |
|-1  1 |

which is not positive definite. This has to do with the transformation from the unconstrained space to the constrained space of a correlation, which utilizes the hyperbolic tangent transformation. If the parameter goes below about -9 in the unconstrained space, then tanh(-9) = 1 as far as the computer knows.

In any event, if this only happens a few times out of thousands of iterations, then you do not need to worry about it. Moreover, you do not need to worry about positive definiteness warnings when the correlation matrix or covariance matrix in question is declared in the parameters block because those matrices are positive definite by construction, even though they may be singular numerically. The informational message is there out of an abundance of caution for people who are constructing their own correlation or covariance matrices in the transformed parameters block and may have made a mistake in the implementation so that the resulting matrix is not positive definite by construction.

Ben
